bullets.title: AAPL: Price hikes confirmed, ~$50 ASP increase expected vs. $200+ press estimates; INTC foundry deal announced
bullets.body: Tim Cook confirmed Apple will raise product prices due to 4x surge in memory/storage costs. JPM (OW, $325 PT) estimates iPhone 18 ASP increases of only ~$50 (mid-single digit %), far below press estimates of $200+, citing ~$40 in component savings and ~$15 from in-house modem integration as offsets; gross margin impact estimated at ~20 bps for total company. Separately, Trump confirmed AAPL agreed to work with INTC on US chip design/manufacturing — analysts view the deal (~5% of TSMC's AAPL business, ~$1-1.2B annually on 18A-P node for Mac) as supply chain diversification; AAPL +2.4% on the week.

bullets.title: INTC: +10.6% on Trump-backed AAPL foundry deal; 18A-P enters risk production
bullets.body: Intel surged ~10-11% after President Trump publicly confirmed AAPL will work with INTC on chip design and US manufacturing. INTC's 18A-P process has entered risk production with estimated production readiness late 2027-2028; Wells Fargo estimates the deal is likely for INTC 18A-P node for Mac series. Analysts view this as a critical validation step for INTC's foundry ambitions.

bullets.title: MU: +15.5% on the week; earnings next Tuesday June 24 as key catalyst
bullets.body: MU was the week's standout performer, up 15.5% driven by upbeat earnings previews and broader DRAM sector strength (DRAM index +18% on the week, semis +7.3%). JPM flags MU earnings on June 24 as the next major catalyst. MS QDS flags MU as carrying the largest single-name short gamma per 1% market move, suggesting elevated realized vol risk around the print.

bullets.title: NVDA: AI rally driver; AMZN developing custom chips to challenge; elevated gamma risk flagged
bullets.body: NVDA was among the top retail and institutional AI beneficiaries this week (retail top-3 YTD buy). Separately, Amazon is in discussions to sell custom AI chips to third parties, presenting a direct competitive challenge to NVDA's data center dominance. MS QDS flags NVDA as one of the largest short-gamma names per 1% move in the US market, alongside MU and TSLA.

bullets.title: MSFT: -2.9% on DeepSeek enterprise risk; MS flags 43% upside to 12m high, -21% YTD
bullets.body: MSFT fell ~2.9% this week as the company is reportedly considering offering DeepSeek as a cheaper enterprise alternative, raising margin and competitive concerns. Morgan Stanley notes MSFT is -21% YTD despite AI monetization tailwinds, with 43% upside to its 12-month high, and recommends low-premium call-spread structures. MSFT also has a significant AI model business in China flagged as a geopolitical risk.

bullets.title: ACN: -~18% on missed guidance and $4B+ dilutive acquisitions; multiple downgrades
bullets.body: Accenture reported FQ3 EPS beat ($3.80 vs. $3.74E) but Q4 revenue guidance of $17.75-18.40B missed the Street's $18.42-18.50B. The company announced ~$4.175B in cybersecurity acquisitions (Dragos, runZero, NetRise) viewed as dilutive near-term. William Blair downgraded to Market Perform (from Outperform) at $127.98. UBS maintains Buy at $275 PT, arguing cybersecurity revenue (~$10B, 35% CAGR since 2016) is underappreciated and Middle East headwinds are being over-discounted. AI-driven disintermediation risk was also cited as an emerging secular concern.

bullets.title: FOXA +20.7% to acquire ROKU +3.9%; deal confirmed in weekly recap
bullets.body: Fox Corp announced an acquisition of Roku this week; FOXA surged 20.7% and ROKU gained 3.9% on the news. No additional terms were provided in the digest items.

bullets.title: TSLA: Top retail buy YTD; elevated short gamma flagged; EU speediness concerns emerging
bullets.body: Tesla ranks among top-3 retail net buys YTD alongside NVDA and MU per MS QDS data. TSLA also carries the largest single-name short gamma exposure per 1% move alongside MU and NVDA, elevating vol risk. Separately, Sweden may oppose Tesla's supervised self-driving technology in Europe over speeding concerns.

bullets.title: SNAP: Specs AR glasses estimated at $3.5B development cost, $500M annual cash burn
bullets.body: Snap's AR Specs product is estimated to have cost $3.5B to develop with $500M in ongoing annual cash burn, according to new reporting cited in afternoon headlines. No analyst rating action accompanied this disclosure.

bullets.title: HOOD: +16.1% on SEC tokenized stocks innovation exemption proposal
bullets.body: Robinhood surged 16.1% this week after the SEC proposed an innovation exemption for tokenized stocks. The broader fintech/non-bank lending complex also rallied, with AFRM +11.7% on constructive master trust card data showing improved delinquency rates and accelerated loan growth.

bullets.title: TLN, CEG, VST: FERC co-location tariff approved, accelerating data center interconnection
bullets.body: FERC approved PJM's revised co-location tariff allowing data centers to contract only for incremental grid load above on-site generation, and issued show-cause orders to RTOs to accelerate interconnection timelines beyond a 2029 target. MS Energy flags TLN, CEG, and VST as primary IPP beneficiaries of the behind-the-meter and co-location framework. ERCOT's Batch 0 (35 GW baseload, 65 GW under study) should provide developer clarity by August 7.

bullets.title: EQIX, DLR: Data center REITs outperform +2.95%; incumbents seen insulated from public opposition
bullets.body: Data center REITs outperformed the broader real estate sector (+2.95%) as AI infrastructure demand narrative remains strong. Despite $130B in projects blocked or delayed in 2026 due to power/water/community concerns, incumbents Equinix and Digital Realty are seen as insulated vs. newer entrants. FERC is accelerating data center grid connections with 90-day approvals, but hyperscalers must fund infrastructure upgrades.

bullets.title: HIMS: Peptides rollout speed and 2027+ upside under investor focus following stock move
bullets.body: Truist notes rising investor interest in HIMS following a significant stock move, with questions centering on potential revenue and EBITDA guidance raises and the speed of the peptides business rollout. 2027+ upside from peptides expansion is highlighted as a key debate point.

bullets.title: DKNG: NY sports betting GGR -23% YTD in 2Q26; FIFA/Knicks negative holds driving miss
bullets.body: DraftKings' NY 2QTD GGR is tracking -23% YoY with handle -1% YoY and market share falling from 35% to 33%. FanDuel similarly -21% YoY. Negative holds were driven by outsized betting volumes on the NY Knicks and Team USA FIFA World Cup victories. Fanatics is the only sportsbook with positive 2QTD GGR (+4% YoY) and is gaining share (+199 bps).

bullets.title: SHOP: AI marketing tool launch; planning ads in ChatGPT and Microsoft ecosystem
bullets.body: Shopify is rolling out an AI tool enabling merchants to run marketing campaigns, and is planning to bring ads into ChatGPT and Microsoft platforms. No analyst rating action accompanied this disclosure.

bullets.title: CSCO: Acquires Widefield Security to strengthen Splunk's Agentic SOC capabilities
bullets.body: Cisco announced intent to acquire Widefield Security (undisclosed terms) to extend Splunk's Agentic SOC with identity and session intelligence for human, non-human, and AI-agent activity at machine speed. This is consistent with Cisco's ongoing post-Splunk integration build-out strategy.

bullets.title: NVDA, MSFT, GOOGL, META, AVGO: MS recommends low-premium AI call hedges for underexposed funds
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley flags significant AI FOMO risk: nearly 20% of global hedge funds have <10% AI exposure and 75% of US mutual funds are below benchmark weight to semis despite semis representing 25% of index weight. MS recommends call-spread collars and knock-out calls on NVDA, MSFT, GOOGL, META, and AVGO given high IV (82% of AI enablers >40v). MSFT is -21% YTD with 43% upside to 12m high; META -19% YTD with 39% upside.

bullets.title: HPE: AI server growth triple-digits YoY; supply-constrained through 2026-2027; Juniper synergies accelerating
bullets.body: HPE is seeing triple-digit server revenue growth YoY driven by refresh cycles and pricing power, with supply constrained through 2026-2027 and backlog expected to grow through year-end. AI inference is projected to grow from 30% to 80%+ of compute by 2030. HPE's Juniper integration is expanding AI networking stack participation across scale-up, scale-out, and scale-across architectures; HPE was also selected by Vultr for next-gen AI infrastructure deployment.

bullets.title: IREN: Initiated Buy at Jefferies; pivot from bitcoin mining to AI infrastructure
bullets.body: Jefferies initiated IREN with a Buy rating, highlighting the company's strategic pivot from bitcoin mining to AI infrastructure as the core thesis.

bullets.title: MU flow setup: SNDK, MU carry largest short gamma per 1% move; levered ETF demand near record
bullets.body: MS QDS end-of-week wrap flags that levered ETF exposure is near record highs (~$20B per 1% SPX move short gamma) with an estimated $26B of demand from rebalancing on Friday. MU and SNDK are specifically identified as the largest single-name short gamma carriers per 1% move alongside NVDA and TSLA, creating elevated VaR shock potential heading into MU's June 24 earnings.
